t: MLC LLM: What MLC LLM Is: One Model, Every Device
title: MLC LLM: What MLC LLM Is: One Model, Every Device
description: MLC LLM takes an open large language model — Llama, Qwen, Phi, Mistral families — and compiles it with TVM Unity into a native app for each platform: an iPhone app using the GPU, an Android app, a browser tab via WebGPU (the WebLLM sibling), or a desktop binary. Instead of serving the model from a data center, the model lives on the device. For denied or air-gapped environments that single property changes everything: the assistant works with no connectivity, and prompts never leave the hardware.
key_facts: Compiles open LLMs via TVM Unity

t: MLC LLM: Model Zoo: Which Models Compile
title: MLC LLM: Model Zoo: Which Models Compile
description: MLC LLM maintains a model zoo of prebuilt configurations for popular open models — Llama 3, Qwen 2.5, Phi, Gemma, Mistral — each with a conversion recipe that turns Hugging Face weights into the MLC format with the right tokenizer, chat template, and quantization settings. The mlc-chat CLI and the model library let you pull a compiled model the way you pull a container image. Because the recipes are open, teams can compile their own fine-tunes with the same tooling, which is how private models reach fielded devices.
key_facts: Prebuilt recipes for Llama, Qwen, Phi, Mistral
Private fine-tunes compile with the same tooling

t: MLC LLM: Quantization: q4f16 and Friends
title: MLC LLM: Quantization: q4f16 and Friends
description: Phones cannot hold 16-bit 8B models comfortably, so MLC LLM quantizes weights — typically to 4-bit integers with 16-bit activations (q4f16), shrinking an 8B model from ~16 GB to ~4-5 GB including the runtime. The quantization is group-wise with per-group scales, preserving quality far better than naive rounding, and the compiler generates kernels that dequantize on the fly in registers. The practical result: a capable assistant that fits in a phone's memory budget and answers at tens of tokens per second.

t: MLC LLM: Your First Compile: mlc-chat on a Laptop
title: MLC LLM: Your First Compile: mlc-chat on a Laptop
description: The hello-world is the mlc-chat CLI: install the package, pull a prebuilt 3B-class model, and chat in the terminal with the model running on your laptop GPU. Under the hood the CLI loads the compiled library, the weights, and the tokenizer, then runs the standard prefill/decode loop. Compile time for a new model is measured in minutes on a decent machine; after that, inference starts instantly. This loop — compile once, chat anywhere — is the whole developer experience in miniature.

t: MLC LLM: TVM Unity Under the Hood
title: MLC LLM: TVM Unity Under the Hood
description: MLC LLM is built on TVM Unity, the next-generation layer of the TVM stack: models are expressed in Relax (an IR designed for dynamic-shape ML programs), optimized with first-class features like disk/offload planning, and lowered to per-platform kernels. Unity's dynamic-shape support is what lets one compiled artifact handle arbitrary prompt lengths. Understanding this layering matters when something is slow: the fix is usually a better schedule or a smarter memory plan, not a bigger device.
key_facts: Built on TVM Unity and the Relax IR
Memory plan proven total before emission

t: MLC LLM: KV-Cache Math: Why Long Context Costs Memory
title: MLC LLM: KV-Cache Math: Why Long Context Costs Memory
description: Every token generated attends to every previous token, and the keys and values are cached to avoid recomputation. For an 8B model at 4k context, the KV cache is on the order of a gigabyte — often bigger than the quantized weights' working set. MLC LLM manages this with paged allocation and sliding-window strategies. The back-of-envelope math (2 × layers × heads × head-dim × bytes × tokens) is the single most useful formula in on-device LLM work: it tells you the longest conversation your device can actually hold.
key_facts: KV cache often exceeds weight memory

t: MLC LLM: WebLLM: LLMs in the Browser via WebGPU
title: MLC LLM: WebLLM: LLMs in the Browser via WebGPU
description: WebLLM is MLC's browser sibling: the same compiled models run inside a web page using WebGPU, with weights cached in the browser. A field laptop with a browser becomes an AI workstation with no install and no server. The security properties are attractive for sensitive work: the page can run fully offline after caching, and prompts stay in the browser's memory. Performance tracks the device's GPU — integrated graphics give modest speeds, discrete GPUs give excellent ones.

t: MLC LLM: Defensive Uses: The Disconnected Assistant
title: MLC LLM: Defensive Uses: The Disconnected Assistant
description: The defensive case for on-device LLMs is straightforward: an assistant that helps with procedures, checklists, and documentation where networks are denied, jammed, or simply absent — and where sending prompts to a cloud would be a policy violation. MLC LLM makes the field laptop, the shipboard terminal, and the forward tablet into capable AI endpoints with zero data exfiltration by construction. The model is vetted once, compiled once, and distributed as a signed bundle.

t: MLC LLM: Structured Output and Tool Schemas
title: MLC LLM: Structured Output and Tool Schemas
description: Field assistants need machine-readable answers, so MLC LLM supports constrained generation: grammars and JSON schemas that force the model's output to parse. A maintenance assistant can be required to emit a valid work-order JSON; a triage assistant a fixed severity enum. This turns the LLM from a chatbot into a reliable component in a larger system — downstream code can trust the shape of the answer even while the content varies.

t: MLC LLM: Debugging: When the Model Is Slow or Wrong
title: MLC LLM: Debugging: When the Model Is Slow or Wrong
description: On-device LLM debugging has two halves: performance (profile prefill vs decode, check memory bandwidth saturation, verify the right kernels were selected) and quality (compare against the fp16 reference on an eval set, check the chat template matches training, verify quantization did not collapse a critical capability). MLC's tooling exposes per-phase timings and the eval harness. The classic gotcha is a mismatched chat template — the model then 'forgets' how to follow instructions, and no amount of tuning fixes a template bug.
key_facts: Diff against fp16 on an eval set
Chat-template mismatch is the classic gotcha

t: MLC LLM: Serving Many Users: Throughput Patterns
title: MLC LLM: Serving Many Users: Throughput Patterns
description: On-device is one user; the same compiled models can also serve many via batching servers. MLC's server patterns use continuous batching — new requests join the decode batch as soon as space frees — maximizing tokens per second per GPU. For tactical deployments, a single rugged server can serve a whole team's assistants over the local network with no outside connectivity. The math to watch is the KV-cache budget times concurrent users.
key_facts: One rugged server serves a team locally

t: MLC LLM: Updates: Shipping New Models to the Field
title: MLC LLM: Updates: Shipping New Models to the Field
description: Models improve, so MLC deployments need an update story: versioned bundles, delta downloads where possible, and rollback to the previous known-good model. The practical discipline is staging — new model on a few devices, eval-gated promotion, fleet-wide rollout — exactly like firmware. Because bundles are content-addressed, a device can verify it received the intended bytes before swapping.

t: MLC LLM: Testing: Evals as Acceptance Gates
title: MLC LLM: Testing: Evals as Acceptance Gates
description: You cannot eyeball LLM quality, so MLC workflows lean on eval sets: fixed prompt collections with scored answers, run against every candidate bundle. The eval delta between fp16 and quantized, between model versions, and between platforms becomes the acceptance language. Teams keep a private eval reflecting their actual tasks — field procedures, not internet trivia — because a model can ace public benchmarks and still fumble the job it was deployed for.

title: MLC LLM: Real-World Pattern: Shipboard Technical Assistant
description: A complete pattern: a rugged server below deck runs the compiled assistant over the ship's LAN; crew query procedures, schematics references, and troubleshooting trees with no satellite link required. The model bundle was vetted ashore, its eval results recorded, and updates arrive on physical media with hash verification. When the ship returns, session attestation logs show which model version answered which questions — the audit trail writes itself.

t: MLC LLM: Mastery: The On-Device LLM Playbook
title: MLC LLM: Mastery: The On-Device LLM Playbook
description: Mastery of MLC LLM means fluency in the constraints: quantization trade-offs, KV-cache budgets, kernel selection, chat templates, and eval-driven acceptance. The advanced moves are custom model recipes, new platform backends, and contributing kernels upstream. The deeper lesson is architectural: once the model lives on the device, the system design inverts — the network becomes the exception, local compute the rule, and privacy a property of physics rather than policy.
key_facts: Fluency in quantization, budgets, templates, evals
